key_insight: Extending characteristic mapping to dissipative equations preserves its fine-scale resolution strategy while enabling applications to Navier–Stokes flows.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support efficient simulation of multiscale turbulent flows across a broad range of Reynolds numbers.
method: Lift scalar evolution equations to paths in a diffeomorphism group, interpreted through optimal transport.
Represent and evolve flow maps using composed spatial interpolants and semi-Lagrangian characteristic mapping.
Use semidirect-product time stepping with an exponential integrator for the log-Jacobian.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-order accuracy and tests on canonical nonlinear dissipative equations, but gives no quantitative errors or runtime comparisons.
watch_item: The promise of turbulence simulation across all Reynolds numbers needs validation beyond the canonical tests described in the abstract.
paper_title: A characteristic mapping method for dissipative evolution equations
